id.description: The unique identifier for the configuration.

type.description: What the folder is. 'project' marks the root of a project: the one meta.json 'run projects' lists. 'app' is a service or sub-app below a project and never gets a row of its own. 'template' is a scaffold.

.*.description: Command to be executed for the routine.

secrets.description: Deprecated: .env.base/.env.<env> loading is replaced by varlock (.env.schema); see the system skill.

base.description: Name of the base environment variables file (e.g., 'base' for .env.base). Defaults to 'base'.

tags.description: Free-form words describing what the project is about. For which projects are worked on together, use 'groups'.

groups.description: Names of the groups this project belongs to: sets of projects worked on together, wherever their folders are. Set on a 'project' meta.json only.

herdr.description: Herdr workspace configuration. A project maps to one herdr workspace. Multiple meta.json files can contribute tabs to the same workspace label (assembled with --all).

label.description: Workspace label (typically the project name). Multiple meta.json files can contribute tabs to the same label.

cwd.description: Working directory for the workspace. If starts with '/', treated as absolute path. Otherwise, relative to meta.json location.

color.description: The project's colour: a mark beside the workspace in herdr's sidebar. Set on the project's own meta.json. Switched on and off for every workspace with 'run herdr colors'.

env.description: Environment variables applied to the workspace as key-value pairs

focus.description: Focus this workspace after init (init never steals focus by default)

label.description: Tab label (prefixed with the app name at init, unless prefix is false)

prefix.description: Prefix the label with the app name. Set false when the label already names the app, to keep the tab row readable in a workspace with many apps.

path.description: Starting directory for all panes in this tab. If starts with '/', treated as absolute path. Otherwise, relative to workspace cwd (the contributing meta.json location by default).

env.description: Environment variables applied to this tab as key-value pairs

focus.description: Focus this tab after the workspace is built

layout.description: Layout mode: 'sections' for hierarchical layouts, 'grid' for predefined arrangements, 'compact' for minimal configuration

herdrPane.description: A herdr pane: where it sits, what it is for, and optionally the routine it usually runs.

name.description: Unique identifier for this pane (used as the pane label)

description.description: How to use this pane (documentation; `routine` is what gets executed)

routine.description: Name of the routine this pane usually runs, from the `routines` of the same meta.json. `run herdr init --start` types `run routine <name>` into the pane; without --start the pane stays an empty shell. One routine per pane: anything else is typed by hand.

profiles.description: Names of the profiles this pane's routine is part of: a profile is a set of routines started together (for example 'web'). A name has no spaces. A pane can be in several profiles. Only meaningful on a pane that names a `routine`. Picked in the dashboard's Open question, or with `run herdr init --start --profile <name>`.

size.description: Size of this pane (e.g., '50%', '30'). In grid/compact layouts, overrides the default proportions (the paired pane gets the complement). In sections, applies when this pane is an item in a section.

path.description: Starting directory for this pane. If starts with '/', treated as absolute path. Otherwise, relative to the tab path. The first pane of a layout always inherits the tab path.

env.description: Environment variables applied to this pane as key-value pairs (split-created panes only)

focus.description: Focus this pane after the workspace is built

zoom.description: Zoom (fullscreen) this pane after the workspace is built; zooming also focuses it

herdrSection.description: A section defines how to split space - either containing panes or other sections

split.description: Split direction: horizontal = split top/bottom, vertical = split left/right

size.description: Size of this section (e.g., '50%', '30'). Only applies when this section is an item in another section.

items.description: Items within this section - can be panes or other sections

herdrGrid.description: Predefined grid layout with auto-fill support for missing panes

type.description: Grid type: single (1 pane), vertical (2 panes left/right), horizontal (2 panes top/bottom), two-by-two (4 panes in 2x2 grid), main-side (1 large left + 2 stacked right)

panes.description: Pane definitions. Missing panes will be auto-generated with default names.

herdrCompact.description: Compact grid layout with minimal configuration. Panes are an ordered array (top-left to bottom-right); each entry is either just a pane name, or an object with a name and a description of how to use the pane.

type.description: Grid type: single (1 pane), vertical (2 panes left/right), horizontal (2 panes top/bottom), two-by-two (4 panes in 2x2 grid), main-side (1 large left + 2 stacked right)

panes.description: Ordered pane definitions (top-left to bottom-right). Each entry is a pane name string, or an object with name and description.
